section.title: Write Equations Given a Slope and \( y \)-Intercept
section.para: We can determine the slope and intercept of a line if the equation is written in slope-intercept form, \( y=mx+b \). Now we will do the reverse—we will start with the slope and \( y \)-intercept and use them to find the equation of the line.
Find the equation of a line with slope \( −1 \) and \( y \)-intercept \( (0,−3) \).

Step 3 - Substitute the values into \( y = mx + b \).
\( y = -1x + -3 \)
\( y = -x-3 \)
The same information can be picked up from a graph of a line.
Find the equation of the line shown in the graph.

Step 1 - Find the slope by counting the rise and run.
\( m=\frac{rise}{run} \)
From \( (0, -4) \) to \( (3,-2) \), the slope is \( m = \frac{2}{3} \).

Step 2 - Find the \( y \)-intercept.
\( y \)-intercept \( (0, -4) \)
\( b = -4 \)

Step 3 - Substitute the values into \( y = mx + b \).
\( y = mx +b \)
\( y = \frac{2}{3} x - 4 \)
section.title: Try It: Write Equations Given a Slope and \( y \)-Intercept

problem.para: Write the equation of the line graphed below in slope-intercept form:

image.alt: This figure has a graph of a straight line on the x y-coordinate plane. The x and y-axes run from negative 8 to 8.

problem.para: Write down your answer, and then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para:
Compare your answer:
Here is how to write the equation of the line in slope-intercept form.

Step 1 - Find the slope by counting the rise and run.
\( m=\frac{rise}{run} \)
From \( (0, 1) \) to \( (5, 4) \), the slope is \( m = \frac{3}{5} \).

Step 2 - Find the \( y \)-intercept.
\( y \)-intercept \( (0, 1) \)
\( b = 1 \)

Step 3 - Substitute the values into \( y = mx + b\).
\( y = mx +b \)
\( y = \frac{3}{5} x + 1 \)
